The company's only method for a consumer to opt out of ADMT is a cookie banner or cookie-consent tool. The CPPA's regulations specifically prohibit that (11 CCR § 7221(c)(4)). The Agency explained in its Final Statement of Reasons why it kept this rule despite pushback: it was "based on its observations in the marketplace of businesses inappropriately using cookie banners or controls" as a substitute for a real ADMT opt-out — the concern is not cookies as such, but businesses burying the ADMT opt-out inside a mechanism built for something else. A cookie banner does not satisfy § 7221(c)'s requirement for a dedicated ADMT opt-out method, regardless of how it is worded. Section 4 addresses whether this company has an opt-out method beyond its cookie tool. (California Privacy Protection Agency, Final Statement of Reasons, CCPA Updates, Cyber, Risk, ADMT, and Insurance Regulations, 11 CCR § 7221(c)(4), Appendix p. 212.)
